Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo earlier — excited to move to the pilot. Attached is the PO (Novaterra-PO-4532.pdf). A couple of questions from our side before we kick off finance: 

1) Novaterra operates two legal entities in the EU, one in Ireland (Novaterra Ltd) and one in Germany (Novaterra GmbH). Which entity will Redwood invoice by default? We need the VAT invoice to be raised to the entity that will remit VAT.

2) We typically do Net60 on enterprise procurement, but for pilots Finance has asked whether we can agree a temporary Net45 for the first 90 days, then reassess. Alternatively, we could do Net30 if there's an early-pay discount.

3) Credit cap — our AP team asked if you can confirm any onboarding credit buffer you offer before we hit a committed spend threshold (they listed ~EUR 75k as an initial limit). If you need a reference or extra docs from us to extend credit, let me know.

Attaching the PO here.

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.inference>

Subject: Re: Payment cadence for pilot + PO attached

Hi Oliver — thanks for sending the PO and for the clear list of asks. Quick responses inline, and then proposed next steps below.

1) Invoice entity: We can invoice either Redwood UK Ltd or Redwood EU Sarl. For EU VAT purposes, to make the VAT claim straightforward we recommend invoicing the entity where the service will be consumed. If Novaterra will record consumption under Novaterra Ltd (Ireland), we will issue invoices to that entity. If you'd like, we can include the VAT registration number for the invoicing entity on every invoice.

2) Net terms: We can accommodate a temporary Net45 for the first 90 days for the pilot. Our standard enterprise window is Net30 / Net45 choices; Net60 typically requires a credit review and contract addendum. Proposal: set Net45 for invoices dated through the pilot (90 days from first invoice), then automatic review. If Novaterra opts for Net60 long-term we'll need a signed payment schedule and a modest committed monthly spend or a deposit.

3) Credit cap / onboarding buffer: We commonly offer an onboarding buffer of EUR 50k while the PO is processing. To extend to EUR 75k we'll need a brief credit intake (basic bank reference + forecasted monthly consumption). If helpful, Marissa can send a short form we use.

Next steps: 
- If you confirm the invoice entity (Ireland or Germany) and accept Net45 for 90 days, we'll: 
  - Send an invoice-sample (Net45) and a one-page payment staircase document that explains the ramp to standard terms.
  - Have Finance (Marissa) send the credit intake form if you want the EUR 75k buffer.

I'll attach the sample invoice and staircase doc.

Cheers,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-invoice-sample-net45.xlsx, Attachment: payment-staircase-onepager.pdf]

Hi Oliver / Chloe,

Dropping in from Finance. Short form attached — it's just four items and a bank reference. If Novaterra can return it, we can expedite increasing the buffer from EUR 50k to EUR 75k within 3 business days.

On VAT invoicing: please confirm which legal entity will be taking the charge (Novaterra Ltd or Novaterra GmbH) + the VAT reg number. If you plan to have intercompany chargebacks, note we can put the invoice to Novaterra Ltd and include a secondary remit-to on the PDF as a note, but VAT reclaimability is tied to the billed entity.

Regarding Net60: If you prefer Net60 from day one, we can do that but it requires: 
- A signed payment schedule addendum,
- A minimum committed monthly spend (we'd request EUR 35k/month during the first 3 months), and
- A credit reference (bank or trade).

We can also offer a small early-pay credit: 1% off invoice if paid within 10 days (Net10 discount) as an alternative.

Marissa Cole
Head of Finance Partnerships, Redwood Inference
